question.text: Write the previous statements in the form of ordered pairs from X to Y.

solution: Read each statement: the first element is the student, the second is the type of book he read.
Student a read science and culture: (a, Science), (a, Culture).
Student b read history: (b, History).
Student c read a literary book: (c, Literature).
Student e read a history book: (e, History).
Student d read nothing, so d is in no pair.
R = {(a, Science), (a, Culture), (b, History), (c, Literature), (e, History)}.

question.text: Represent a set of the ordered pairs in the form of an arrow diagram.

answers.answer: An arrow diagram from X = {a, b, c, d, e} to Y = {Science, Literature, Culture, History} with 5 arrows: a→Science, a→Culture, b→History, c→Literature, e→History.
solution: Draw two closed curves. Write X = {a, b, c, d, e} in the left one and Y = {Science, Literature, Culture, History} in the right one.
Mark a point for each element.
Draw an arrow from a to Science and another from a to Culture.
Draw an arrow from b to History.
Draw an arrow from c to Literature.
Draw an arrow from e to History.
Draw no arrow from d, because d read no book.
This gives the 5 arrows, one for each ordered pair of R.

checks.resolve_answer: Arrow diagram with X = {a, b, c, d, e} on the left and Y = {Science, Literature, Culture, History} on the right. Arrows: a→Science, a→Culture, b→History, c→Literature, e→History. d has no arrow.

question.text: Is R a subset from the cartesian product $X \times Y$?

solution: R = {(a, Science), (a, Culture), (b, History), (c, Literature), (e, History)}.
X × Y is the set of all ordered pairs whose first projection is in X and whose second projection is in Y.
In every pair of R, the first element (a, b, c or e) belongs to X.
In every pair of R, the second element (Science, Culture, History or Literature) belongs to Y.
So every pair of R is in X × Y, and R ⊂ X × Y.
Yes, R is a subset of X × Y.

checks.resolve_answer: Yes. Every ordered pair in R = {(a, Science), (a, Culture), (b, History), (c, Literature), (e, History)} has its first element in X and its second element in Y, so $R \subset X \times Y$.

question.text: If $X=\{1,2,3\}$, $Y=\{12,21,47,52\}$, and R is the relation from X to Y where a R b means: (a is a digit from the digits of b), for each $a\in X$, $b\in Y$.
question.stem: Write R and represent it by an arrow diagram and also, by a cartasian diagram.

answers.answer: R = {(1, 12), (1, 21), (2, 12), (2, 21), (2, 52)}. Arrow diagram: 1→12, 1→21, 2→12, 2→21, 2→52, and no arrow from 3. Cartesian diagram: 5 points at these pairs.
solution: For each a in X, find the b in Y that has a as one of its digits.
a = 1: 1 is a digit of 12 and 21. This gives (1, 12) and (1, 21).
a = 2: 2 is a digit of 12, 21 and 52. This gives (2, 12), (2, 21) and (2, 52).
a = 3: 3 is not a digit of any number in Y, so there is no pair.
Arrow diagram: draw X = {1, 2, 3} on the left and Y = {12, 21, 47, 52} on the right. Draw arrows 1→12, 1→21, 2→12, 2→21, 2→52. Draw no arrow from 3, and none to 47.
Cartesian diagram: draw a horizontal axis for X with 1, 2, 3 and a vertical axis for Y with 12, 21, 47, 52.
Mark the 5 points (1, 12), (1, 21), (2, 12), (2, 21), (2, 52). Mark no point above 3.

checks.resolve_answer: R = {(1, 12), (1, 21), (2, 12), (2, 21), (2, 52), (3, ...)}: no, correctly R = {(1, 12), (1, 21), (2, 12), (2, 21), (2, 52)}. Arrow diagram from X = {1, 2, 3} to Y = {12, 21, 47, 52}: 1→12, 1→21, 2→12, 2→21, 2→52. 3 has no arrow and 47 receives none. Cartesian diagram: points plotted at (1,12), (1,21), (2,12), (2,21), (2,52), with X on the horizontal axis and Y on the vertical axis.

question.text: If $X=\{1,2,3\}$, $Y=\{12,21,47,52\}$, and R is the relation from X to Y where a R b means: (a is a digit from the digits of b), for each $a\in X$, $b\in Y$.
question.stem: Show which of the following relations are correct and why? 1 R 52, 2 R 21, 3 R 47

answers.answer: Only 2 R 21 is correct; 1 R 52 and 3 R 47 are not correct.
solution: A relation a R b is correct when (a, b) belongs to R, that is when a is a digit of b.
1 R 52: the digits of 52 are 5 and 2. 1 is not one of them, so it is not correct, and (1, 52) is not in R.
2 R 21: the digits of 21 are 2 and 1. 2 is one of them, so it is correct, and (2, 21) is in R.
3 R 47: the digits of 47 are 4 and 7. 3 is not one of them, so it is not correct, and (3, 47) is not in R.
Only 2 R 21 is correct.

checks.resolve_answer: 1 R 52 is not correct, because 1 is not a digit of 52. 2 R 21 is correct, because 2 is a digit of 21. 3 R 47 is not correct, because 3 is not a digit of 47.
